title: Governance profile cost separation
outOfScope: Rewriting historical archived Work Items or changing provider configuration.
Running release verification for non-release Strict Work Items.

sources.reason: WI-10 outcome, canonical profiles, and cost-separation requirements.
Confirms release as an operation-triggered Strict escalation rather than a fourth profile.
Current routing policy, canonical profile boundary, and release operation escalation behavior.

riskAssessment.reason: Separating intensity from release operation can omit release evidence or overrun non-release Strict work if normalization and derivation drift.

reasons: The router, contract schema, required-evidence derivation, and Make dispatch are governance boundaries.

executionDecision.reason: The user confirmed the three-profile model and release escalation policy.

preReviewWarnings: Review legacy release rejection and automatic release-context derivation, especially omitted operationClasses.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Only light, standard, and strict are accepted governance profiles; legacy release profile input is rejected and release remains an explicit operation class.
The verification graph derives from profile, operation classes, resource claims, and capability claims, with release preflight and distribution checks only for release context.
Release-owned scope, requested operation, or release_ready/distribution_verified claims automatically require release escalation even when omitted by an Agent.
Focused tests prove non-release Strict work excludes release checks, release behavior is preserved, and insufficient release evidence blocks release claims.
Current documentation distinguishes governance intensity from operation-specific verification without rewriting historical archive records.
guidelines: Keep light, standard, and strict as the only canonical profile vocabulary in active routing and documentation.
Reject legacy release profile input while preserving release operation-class escalation.
Derive release escalation conservatively from operation, scope, resources, and claims; no Contract omission may downgrade it.
Keep release-specific gates separate from non-release Strict execution and document the distinction.

intent.problem: Legacy Lite/Standard/Strict/Release routing conflates governance intensity with release operation, making light work insufficiently distinct and risking either skipped release evidence or unnecessary release verification.
constraints: Use only light, standard, and strict as canonical profiles.
Treat release as an explicit Strict escalation, not a profile.
Preserve current release behavior through automatic derivation without legacy profile compatibility.
Do not rewrite historical archive records or modify provider configuration.
intent.rationale: A two-axis model lets low-risk work stay light while release-specific proof remains mandatory whenever the operation or claim requires it.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: light documentation work uses the light graph
scenarioCoverage.expected: Light routes to focused verification without Standard or Strict groups.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: non-release Strict work excludes release graphs
scenarioCoverage.expected: Security or CI scope remains Strict without release_preflight or distribution escalation.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run routing and Make dispatch tests.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Release scopes, operations, and claims add release_preflight and distribution even when the Contract omits them.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: legacy release profile input is rejected
scenarioCoverage.expected: Release must be declared as an operation class, not selected as a governance profile.

rawUserRequest: Complete WI-10 using light, standard, strict profiles and release operation escalation.
